FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Who Works at My School flashcards.

The people who make a school day work, card by card. Sixteen of them stand on these pages: the ones at the front of the room, the ones behind the lunch counter and the library shelf, and the ones at the doors, on the road and on the playground who keep the whole day safe. Every card is right here — what the job is, a game to play tonight and a download button for printing.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page, and every card shows its age pill — start with the group that fits your child today.

People who teach

The faces at the front of the room: one for books, one for paint, one for songs, one for experiments, one for running games — and the student, because the school is really there for them.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Guess who I am

    Pick a card, act the job out — point at an invisible board, hold an invisible STOP sign, steer a big wheel — and let your child guess. Then swap roles. Acting a job is how a child understands it.

  2. 02

    Thank-you round

    Spread five cards on the floor and ask: who would you thank for today? The cook for the apple, the bus driver for the ride, the gardener for the flowers. Gratitude gets concrete when it has a face.

  3. 03

    Who fixes this?

    Ask little problems and let your child slap the right card: a wobbly tooth (nurse), a squeaky door (janitor), a dry plant (gardener), an empty tummy (cafeteria worker). Fast rounds, big giggles.

  4. 04

    Walk the school story

    Lay the cards out in the order your child meets them on a real day: crossing guard, teacher, cafeteria worker, playground supervisor, bus driver. Every school has its own story — walk your child’s.

      Teacher Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who teach

      A teacher is the grown-up who shows you new things at school — letters, numbers, songs, how to wait for a turn — and helps when something feels tricky.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Teacher! This is my teacher. She shows me new things and helps me try. Look how she points at the board — that is where the new stuff lives!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play teacher at home: your child at a chair-and-paper "board", you and three stuffed animals as the class. Practice raising a hand, listening for the claps, lining up at the door. The child in the teacher’s shoes stops worrying about the real ones.

      Quick parent note

      A teacher is often the first grown-up outside the family your child listens to every day. Naming the teacher by name — "Ms. Alvarez" — turns this card into a real, safe person.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Art Teacher Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who teach

      An art teacher is the grown-up who brings out the paint, the glue, the crayons and the big paper — and shows you how an idea turns into a picture.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Art teacher! Paint, brushes, glue — and look, an easel! The art teacher says every picture is a good picture. Mine has a purple mountain!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Make a two-minute gallery: hang three of your child’s drawings with painter’s tape, walk them like a museum and clap for each one. "The artist" loves an audience.

      Quick parent note

      Art class is where a child learns that trying beats tidy. If your child comes home splattered, that is the lesson working — the washing machine has your back.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Music Teacher Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who teach

      A music teacher is the grown-up who brings the songs, the rhythm sticks, the drums and the guitar — and shows you that your voice is an instrument too.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Music teacher! A guitar! We sing loud, we sing quiet, we clap — boom boom! The music teacher knows a song about EVERYTHING.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Start an echo song at dinner: you sing two words, your child echoes them, then swap leader. Real music class runs on exactly this game — the leader-and-echo habit transfers on day one.

      Quick parent note

      Songs are memory glue — the tidy-up song really does work. Ask your child to teach you one school song; being the teacher at home is a confidence snack.

      Science Teacher Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who teach

      A science teacher is the grown-up who sets up the experiments — magnets, magnifiers, seeds, bubbles — and treats every "but why?" like the best question of the day.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Science teacher! A flask — careful, clever! We look, we guess, we try it. Why does the magnet stick? Let’s find out!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Do one kitchen experiment: sink or float. Fill a bowl with water, gather five small things, guess first, then drop them in. Guessing-then-testing IS science — the science teacher would absolutely approve.

      Quick parent note

      At three to five, science is a habit, not facts: look, guess, try. "I don’t know — let’s find out" is the sentence the science teacher wants every child to steal.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      PE Teacher Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who teach

      A PE teacher is the grown-up who plans the running, jumping, balancing and ball games — the part of school where your whole body gets to work.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “PE teacher! Whistle — tweet! We run, we jump, we balance. Gym day is the loudest, fastest day of school!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Animal races down the hallway: hop like a bunny, waddle like a duck, stomp like an elephant, freeze at the whistle (any word works). Real PE runs on listen-then-move — this practices exactly that.

      Quick parent note

      PE builds more than muscles: taking turns, waiting for a whistle, trying again after a fall. Sneakers on gym day save tears — mark the day on the calendar together.

      Student Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who teach

      A student is someone who learns at school — and on this card, that is your child. The whole school is really there for the students.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “A student! That is ME! I sit at my desk, I listen, I try, I learn. The school is full of helpers — and they are all there for me.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play "first day of school" with the card: backpack on, walk to the door, wave goodbye, big hello when you come back. Practicing the day-in, day-out rhythm makes the real one feel known.

      Quick parent note

      Being a student is your child’s actual job — maybe their first one. Asking "what did you DO today?" asks about their work; asked warmly, that question builds a student’s pride.

      School Nurse Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who help

      A school nurse is the helper who looks after children when they feel sick or get a scrape — she checks, bandages and sits with you until you feel better.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “School nurse! If I feel yucky or scrape my knee, the nurse helps me. A cool bandage, a drink of water, a sit-down — and soon I am playing again.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Bandage the teddy: one bandage, one worried teddy, one gentle nurse (your child). Practicing "check it, clean it, bandage it, all better" makes a real trip to the nurse feel like a known story.

      Quick parent note

      Tell your child the nurse is a safe grown-up for hard moments — a person who helps when you cannot be there. That sentence is a superpower on the days you are apart.

      Librarian Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who help

      A librarian is the person who looks after the library — finding the right book, reading it aloud and knowing just which story to hand you next.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Librarian! So many books — up high and down low! The librarian finds the best one: about diggers? About bears? Here you go!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play librarian at your own shelf: five books face-out, your child behind the "desk" and every stuffed animal asking for a book by name. Pretend checkouts build real library manners.

      Quick parent note

      The librarian is a reading matchmaker — a child who says "I want a book about trucks" gets one, and that yes is how readers start. Try the same question at your public library; librarians there love it.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Cafeteria Worker Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who help

      A cafeteria worker is the person who cooks and serves school lunch — the friendly face behind the counter who hands over the tray.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Cafeteria worker! Lunch is ready — tray, spoon, apple! "Apple or banana?" — I choose, and I say thank you!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Cafeteria night at home: your child takes orders behind the counter and serves the family (real or pretend trays). Serving food is power-role play — picky eaters often taste more when they are the chef.

      Quick parent note

      Lunchtime is a social lesson on a tray: choosing, saying please and thank you, carrying a tray, sitting with friends. Naming the person who serves it turns the lunch line from a crowd into a face.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Janitor Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who help

      A janitor is the person who keeps the school clean and working — mopping floors, fixing squeaky doors, making the whole building ready for tomorrow.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Janitor! Squeak, squeak — the mop! He fixes the door, cleans the spill, keeps our school shiny. What a job!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Be the cleanup crew: one song, ten minutes, everything back in its basket — then admire the room the way the janitor would. Clean-up feels like a job people do, not a punishment, when it has a name.

      Quick parent note

      Every school has people doing quiet work the whole day depends on. Pointing at the janitor and saying "the school works because of him too" plants respect for every kind of job — a big idea from one small card.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      School Gardener Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who help

      A school gardener is the person who tends the school plants — watering, planting seeds and showing children how a seed turns into something to eat.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “School gardener! Watering can — sprinkle, sprinkle! Seeds drink water, sunshine does the rest, and one day — a tomato! A carrot! A bean!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Adopt one plant — a bean in a cup on the windowsill works. Your child waters it, checks it, maybe measures it with a crayon. Watching a seed wake up is the longest, best yes in childhood.

      Quick parent note

      Gardens teach waiting, which is a hard skill at three. A gardener-tended plant gives your child daily proof that small, boring care — water, water, water — becomes something amazing.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Principal Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who keep us safe

      A principal is the person who leads the school — the one who makes sure the classrooms, the teachers and the playground all run well, and whose office door is open.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “The principal! The friendly boss of the whole school. If something is wonderful — or something is wrong — the principal’s door is open. Come in!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Wave-at-the-principal week: at every pickup, one friendly wave or hello by name. A principal who is a known, smiling person stops being The Scary Office forever.

      Quick parent note

      Children sometimes hear "principal’s office" as a scary place. Flip it: the principal is the school’s biggest problem-solver, and the office is where good ideas and good hellos happen.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Security Guard Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who keep us safe

      A security guard is the person who watches the school’s doors and gates — who comes in, who goes out — so everyone inside stays safe.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Security guard! He watches the gate and the doors — careful and kind. Only the right people come in. That is how we all stay safe!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Gatekeeper game: one child (or a teddy) is the guard at a doorway with a list of who may pass — "bears, yes; dinosaurs, hmm, show me your ticket!" Being the gatekeeper builds understanding instead of fear.

      Quick parent note

      Security work can feel invisible or scary. The card makes the guard a person with a job: watch, check, welcome the right people. That framing lets a child feel watched-over instead of watched.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Crossing Guard Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who keep us safe

      A crossing guard is the helper at the road crossing who holds up the STOP sign and gets children across safely — before and after school.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Crossing guard! STOP — the sign goes up! Cars wait, feet cross, safe on the other side. Wave thank you — every single day!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Red light, green light, crossing-guard edition: your child holds a paper STOP sign and decides when the teddy bears may cross the "road" (a rug works). Holding the sign makes the rule make sense.

      Quick parent note

      The crossing guard is a road-safety teacher in a vest. Practice the real ritual: stop at the curb, wait for the sign, look left-right-left, cross, say thank you. The thank-you is part of the safety.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Bus Driver Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who keep us safe

      A bus driver is the person who drives the school bus — bringing children to school in the morning and taking them home again, safe and sound.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Bus driver! Beep, beep! He knows every stop, every name, every bump in the road. On the bus we sit down, we hold on, we ride home!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Bus pretend: line up kitchen chairs, assign stops (Teddy Street, Dolly Corner) and take turns driving and riding. Practice the two bus rules that matter most: bottoms on seats, wait for the driver’s nod before standing.

      Quick parent note

      The bus driver is the first and last face of the school day for riders. Knowing the driver — and being known by them — is real comfort for children who ride. "Mr. Lee drives MY bus" is big-scale belonging.

      FLASHCARD · WHO WORKS AT MY SCHOOL · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Playground Supervisor Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+People who keep us safe

      A playground supervisor is the grown-up who watches over recess — keeping the games fair, the slides safe and every child seen.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Playground supervisor! Whistle — tweet! The games are fair, the line for the slide is moving, and everyone gets a turn. Play on!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Playground-spotting: at any park, ask your child to find the watching grown-up first (every playground has one). Naming the watcher — at school or at the park — is the safety habit itself.

      Quick parent note

      Recess is the hardest curriculum of the day: sharing, waiting, big feelings. The supervisor is there so children can practice freely — and knowing who that person is makes help easy to ask for.
